summary.intent: Fix DatePicker showing the previous day after a user manually selects a date while the browser is in a UTC+ (east-of-UTC) timezone, per the originating issue bokeh/bokeh#9129 and the supplied review packet for bokeh/bokeh#9232.
summary.issue_fit: Met for the reported UTC+ post-selection scenario, but the same helper's blanket timezone-offset correction introduces a symmetric one-day error for UTC- (west-of-UTC) users on the widget's most basic path — initial `value`, `min_date`, `max_date` — see finding `date-picker/tz-offset-regression`.
summary.coverage: Both changed files read in full. `_unlocal_date` traced end to end together with its Python-side serialization source (`bokeh/core/property/datetime.py`, `bokeh/util/serialization.py`), and its exact diff logic reproduced with scratch Node scripts under five timezones (Europe/Paris, Europe/London, America/New_York, America/Los_Angeles, UTC), independently re-verified by a second, fresh-context pass.
check_details: Reviewer-executed: scratch Node trace of `_unlocal_date` exactly as it appears in the diff, for both the post-selection local-date-string input and the server-supplied UTC-midnight input, under TZ=Europe/Paris, Europe/London, America/New_York, America/Los_Angeles, UTC — confirms the intended fix and an independently reproduced new regression.

Unavailable: tests/integration/widgets/test_datepicker.py is a Selenium integration suite; no browser, Selenium, or network is available in this sandbox, so it was not executed. Settled instead by tracing its assertions against the reproduced `_unlocal_date` behavior.

findings.title: Stop shifting server-supplied dates across the day boundary
findings.trigger: A user whose browser timezone has a positive `getTimezoneOffset()` (west of UTC, e.g. `America/New_York` or `America/Los_Angeles` — most of the Americas) opens a `DatePicker` whose `value`, `min_date`, or `max_date` came from Python as a `datetime.date`. `bokeh/util/serialization.py:184` (`convert_datetime_type`) serializes that to an exact UTC-midnight timestamp, which is precisely the originating issue's own repro, `DatePicker(value=datetime.date.today())`.
findings.impact: `_unlocal_date` now unconditionally subtracts `getTimezoneOffset()*60000` ms before reading the calendar day. For a UTC-midnight instant and a positive offset this rolls the instant back into the previous UTC day, so `defaultDate`/`minDate`/`maxDate` display and bound one day earlier than the real value. Node trace on `Date.UTC(2019,0,15,0,0,0)` under `TZ=America/New_York` (and `America/Los_Angeles`): merge-base prints `Tue Jan 15 2019`, head prints `Mon Jan 14 2019` — the same class of off-by-one-day bug this PR fixes, now hitting the opposite hemisphere of timezones on every initial render and on `min_date`/`max_date` always.
findings.change: Apply the offset correction only to a date built from the post-selection local-midnight string (the `_on_select` round trip via `date.toDateString()`), not to a date that already denotes an exact instant supplied by the server, so the calendar day for `defaultDate`/`minDate`/`maxDate` survives unmodified in every timezone.

findings.title: Exercise _unlocal_date at a non-UTC offset in the new tests
findings.trigger: The Selenium suite runs with no `TZ` override, so it executes at the host's default offset (UTC in ordinary CI).
findings.impact: At a UTC offset of zero, `_unlocal_date`'s merge-base and head logic are byte-identical (confirmed by Node trace), so `test_js_on_change_executes` and `test_server_on_change_round_trip` pass identically whether or not the fix -- or the regression above -- is present, giving no regression protection for the defect this PR addresses.
findings.change: Add a case, or parametrize the existing ones, to run with `TZ` set to a non-UTC offset in each direction (e.g. `Europe/Paris` and `America/New_York`) and assert the displayed/selected date there too.

observations.fact: `_unlocal_date` mutates its `date` argument in place via `setTime`, which is harmless today only because every call site passes a freshly constructed `Date`.

requirements.evidence: Node trace of bokehjs/src/lib/models/widgets/date_picker.ts:78-88 under TZ=Europe/Paris and TZ=Europe/London: the post-selection re-render now shows the clicked day instead of the day before, matching issue bokeh/bokeh#9129's repro.

tests/integration/widgets/test_datepicker.py adds 3 Selenium tests, left unchecked as unverified in the PR body; unexecuted here (Selenium/browser unavailable), and per finding date-picker/tests-timezone-blind they run at TZ=UTC, where they cannot discriminate the fix (or the regression) from the pre-fix code.
